doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: How the Los Angeles scene changed and his daily routine
summary: Synthesizers cut studio work; he works little clubs and practices daily.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: How has the L.A. scene changed since when you first moved out here?

I just think mostly the studio scene is, for myself, not as plentiful. Very little, because of the synthesizers, one guy is doing all the work of maybe an orchestra or so on. So I don’t know if it’s changed so much except that fell off, the studio work and pictures and things like that. I seem to be working more at little jazz clubs or little gigs lately for some reason so that’s good. My girlfriend says, “You must be playing good.”
That’s good to hear. So I keep trying to stay interested in music, at least do a little, say hello to the instruments every day.
Say hello to the instruments every day.
Or else they get mad you know. They say, “You haven’t touched me for a few days, you think I’m going to play good?”
You think I’m going to respond to you?

You think I’m going to respond to you, yeah. And I spent a lot of time at the piano. Just like you do I like to look at either books or my own thing, either piano technique or mostly harmonies and what you could do with the chords. Same thing over again.
Do you travel out from L.A. much these days?
Not too much except the surrounding things like Palm Springs occasionally or just within a fifty mile radius or if I go out to Japan.
